chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali al-Washshā, from Aḥmad ibn ‘Ā’idh, from Abū Khadījah, from a man who asked Abū Ja‘far (peace be upon him) about the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him).
He said: 'It is equal to one Hajj and one ‘Umrah.' And he said with his hand like this [stretching it out] — this much of the good. He said with both of his hands like this.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Ja‘far (Imam al-Bāqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.زِيَارَةِ: Ziyarah (visitation, specifically of graves of Imams and prophets)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyarah to the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) equates the spiritual merit of visiting Imam al-Husayn’s (a.s.) grave with the combined reward of Hajj and ‘Umrah, emphasizing its supreme status in Shia devotional practice. The Imam’s gesture of spreading both hands signifies the boundless and comprehensive nature of this reward, reflecting the theological view that Ziyarah serves as a means of reconnecting with the Ahl al-Bayt’s legacy and attaining divine proximity.
